data.gender_notes: Hymen is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From Greek hymenos, hymen, threshold, door, or wedding veil. In ancient Greek culture, a bride would step over a hymen, a threshold or veil, to symbolize the transition to married life. In Christianity, the hymen is a symbol of purity and innocence, particularly associated with the Virgin Mary. The name Hymen carries the meaning “Threshold, Wedding” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hymen usually hope their child will grow to embody threshold, wedding and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Ὑμεν
in_greek.long_meaning: From the ancient Greek word 'ὑμνέω' (hymneō) which means 'to sing a hymn, to make a vow, to swear an oath, to celebrate a wedding, or to make a covenant'. In ancient Greek culture, Hymen was the god of marriage and was invoked during weddings to ensure a successful union. The veil worn by the bride during the wedding ceremony was also called a 'hymen' and symbolized the bride's virginity.
